_what_this_is: The external pin on the law's own bytes AND on everything that decides whether the law runs or what it reads. ROUND 49 (CD-48-01) pinned the two law files: the caller could no longer skip the audit, because any edit to the law moved a digest here. ROUND 50 closes the two rungs above that, both measured as fail-opens. The coordinator's CD-49-01 (P1): nothing pinned COLLECTION, so one line in vitest.config.ts, one flag in package.json's test script, or a testNamePattern left the law uncollected with a green suite and an untouched pin (278 passed with a plant); the pin now covers vitest.config.ts, package.json, both tsconfigs and every tools/ file the law executes, and tools/law-ran.py runs OUTSIDE the suite as its own npm script and refuses by name (LAW-NOT-RUN) when the law's cases did not run. The challenger's R48-F3 (P1): nothing pinned what the law READS as configuration, so one appended enrolment line in tools/reviewer-reports.json exempted a planted document at 303 passed — camouflaged as the bookkeeping every round does — so that file is pinned here, its entries must be reviewer-shaped names carrying a sha256, and an enrolled report's bytes are verified against it. ROUND 51 closes the rung above BOTH of those, the coordinator's CD-50-01 (P1): a gate in its own script is a gate nobody runs. With the law's two files excluded in vitest.config.ts, `npm test` printed 277 passed and exited 0 WITH A PLANT PRESENT, because the pin check lived in an excluded file and nothing called `gate:law` — not `test`, and there is no CI for this package. The law gate is now chained into the command people actually run (`test` is `vitest run && python3 -I tools/law-ran.py`), the pin covers that package.json, and the law reads the SCRIPT NAMES that reach the gate and refuses REFUSED-TEST-DOES-NOT-RUN-THE-LAW when `test` is not one of them. R49-S1 (P3), the challenger's, rides the same commit: `tools/pack-set.json` was the one file of the configuration class still outside this pin, and an unpinned edit to it changes the gate's SUBJECT SET, so it is pinned here too — for the class, not for a measured hole (the challenger's attack on it reds anyway, 1 failed | 302 passed). THE DECLARED LIMIT, unchanged in shape: an edit to a pinned file AND to this pin together passes, bounded by review of the diff, where it is a changed digest sitting beside the change it licenses. WHERE THAT BOUND DOES NOT HOLD, measured at R51-F1 and written here because the sentence above would otherwise overstate it: if the edit also stops the pin's READER from being collected — which one edit to package.json's test script does — then no digest changes at all and the diff shows that one file alone. The bound is review of the diff, not a guarantee that a digest line appears in it. A PIN CANNOT PIN ITSELF: this file's own bytes are not hashed here, and what stands in for that is the SET check on both sides (dropping a row refuses by name in both files) plus that same review. Updating a digest here is a deliberate act with a visible diff line, and the commit message must say why.
